title: Preface
summary: Table of contents for a February 1985 CIA working paper on Coordinate Remote Viewing, covering Stages I through VI and beyond. It lists chapters on introduction, ideograms, each stage, a sample session, future stages, conclusions, and a glossary. The text is mostly OCR residue and release-stamp header noise, so little substantive content is present.

title: CHAPTER ONE INTRODUCTION
summary: Introduces Coordinate Remote Viewing (CRV) training, divided into six sequential stages (Major Gestalt, Sensory Contact, Dimension/Motion/Mobility, General Qualitative Analytical Aspects, Specific Analytical Aspects, Three-Dimensional Contact/Modeling), each taught via theory and practical exercises before advancing. Explains the problem of Analytical Overlay (AOL) and fill-in-the-blanks distortion, the SRI-International signal/noise model, and an idealized skill-learning curve with a first-time effect, decline, and plateau. Notes training duration is variable and individual, and that later stages are covered in chapter 10.

title: CHAPTER 2 IDEOGRAMS
summary: Chapter 2 introduces CRV ideograms: the viewer's kinesthetic response to a site's coordinate, the foundation of Stage I training. An ideogram has three parts: a squiggle drawn spontaneously, an A- feeling/motion (five feeling categories: solid, liquid, airiness, energy, temperature; plus motion descriptors), and a B- automatic analytical response (e.g., land, water), written as 'no B' if none. Four types are described: single, double, composite, and multiple, with examples. The chapter notes that viewers must not interpret visual appearance, and it sets up later chapters.

title: CHAPTER 3 STAGE I MAJOR GESTALT
summary: Describes Stage I of the CRV (Controlled Remote Viewing) training program, centered on 'structure,' the viewer's controlled process for objectifying signal data. Covers the interviewer-viewer interaction kept minimal, the ideogram sequence (I, A-feeling/motion, B-analytical response) moving from gestalt to detail, session setup (name, location, date/time, coordinates), recording personal inclemencies (PI), and three session classes (A operational, B confirmation, C/G training with feedback). Explains feedback codes (Site, Correct, Probably Correct, Near, Can't Feed-back, no negative feedback), summaries, and breaks: Break, Miss Break, AOL Break, AOL-D Break, BILO Break, TM Break, and CONF Break. Stage I has two phases: single large gestalts, then detailed sites.

title: CHAPTER 4 STAGE II SENSORY CONTACT
summary: Stage II of CRV describes sensory contact: after the signal line widens, viewers receive basic bodily sensations (tastes, smells, textures, sounds, colors, temperatures, energies like magnetics or radiation). These 'Stage IIs' arrive in clusters after decoding the ideogram, are recorded as 'S-2' in column form, and generate little analysis. Single ones are 'floating Stage IIs' and less reliable. Expanded aperture leads to dimensionals (Stage III) and aesthetic impact.

title: CHAPTER 5 STAGE IIT MOTION, AND MOBILITY

summary: Chapter 5 of a CRV (Controlled Remote Viewing) training text covers Stage III: its goal of total command of structure and five elements. These are Aesthetic Impact (emotional reaction to the site, declared as AI Break), Enhanced Dimensional Contact (line, plane, solid, horizontal/vertical/diagonal, mass, volume, space), Motion and Mobility, Trackers (dot-drawn outlines from autonomic perception), and Sketches (analytic versus spontaneous, with spontaneous ideograms checked for A and B). It also describes the prompt sequence and passive cuing. Completion requires a rendering, three dimensionals, an AI debrief, mobility, and a tracker or sketch, all with proper structure control.

title: CHAPTER 6 STAGE IV GENERAL QUALITATIVE ANALYTICAL ASPECTS
summary: Describes Stage IV of a remote-viewing training session: it moves beyond physical site description to activities, objects, and feelings, and trainees sort incoming data into eight columns: S-2 (sensations similar to Stage II), Dimensionals (physical size), Aesthetic Impact (closed-ended, followed by a break), Emotional Impact (open-ended, slow, no break), Tangibles (touchable things), Intangibles (non-touchable concepts), AOL (closed-ended, followed by a break), and AOL From the Signal (pre-visual, no break). Covers the handwritten matrix, balancing data flow across columns, sketching and debriefing sketches, and completion criteria (sufficient data with session control), while warning not to analyze data, which would produce AOL; Stage V addresses interrogating signals for detail.

title: CHAPTER 7 STAGE V
summary: Describes Stage V of a remote-viewing analytical method: interrogating the signal line to reveal categories (objects, attributes, subjects, topics) without producing AOL (analytical overlay). Explains prompting with categories and requesting 'emanations' to elicit raw signal, shifting categories as data flows, using 'prior emanations' to look through AOL, and the difficulty of distinguishing subjects from topics. Stage V is best started when Stage IV slows, and it prepares the viewer for Stage VI 3D modeling. Includes a US Grants Farm example, with the rest of the text garbled OCR.

title: CHAPTER 8 STAGE VI THREE DIMENSIONAL CONTACT AND MODELING
summary: A Stage VI guide describes three-dimensional modeling of a site using clay or other materials, built by feel rather than sketching, to aid analysts (e.g., locating a hostage building); it recommends practice before sessions, notes the stage is an enjoyable culmination of training, and previews follow-on CRV stages. A sample session (Stages I-VI, Feb 1985) describes a pyramid-shaped, massive, gray stone temple with Indian/Mexican cultural attributes, concluding with identification of the Mayan Temple at Tulum, Mexico, with a figure of the Tulum ruins.

title: CHAPTER 10 FUTURE STAGES
summary: Chapter 10 outlines the author's personal speculative future stages of psychic development (CRV) from three and a half years of training, presented as a natural continuum, not trainable. Stage VII is Analytics (recognizing numbers/letters, yes/no decisions, developed by I. Swann). Stage VIII is Phonetics/Sonics (producing sounds like 'Carribah' tied to persons, places, things). Stage IX is Telepathic Signals, in two phases: receiving and transmitting, building on emotional impact (EI). Stage X is Remote Action (psychokinesis) in three phases: affecting things, teleporting things from the site, and bringing them back. Stage XI is altering dimensionality/time at the site, possibly freezing, advancing, or reversing time, with phases for each added dimension.

title: CHAPTER 11 CONCLUSIONS
summary: Conclusions of a CRV (Controlled Remote Viewing) training program after four years: it is now a usable instructional program, but training time could be shortened with a dedicated group that understands CRV. Future stages and improvements are expected, limited only by the imagination of practitioners. Personnel should keep an open mind and pursue new, sometimes radical ideas, which may yield the greatest long-run gains. A viewer's failure stemmed from disbelief, illustrating that people establish their own realities.

title: APPENDIX
summary: A glossary of terms from a CIA document (Approved For Release 2000/08/07, CIA-RDP96-00788R001000400001-7) defining remote-viewing/signal-line terms: AOL (analytical overlay) and AOL-Drive, aesthetic impact, analysis, automatic, aware, break, can't feed-back, confusion, correct, feeling motion, gestalt, idea, ideogram, impact, interrogate, miss, near, noiseless, objectify, objective, peacocking, perception, probably correct, signal, site, stage, structure, too much, unconscious. Defines codes CFB, CON, C, N, PC, S, TM and the interviewer and viewer roles.
